hypothesis: Replacing whole-frame / scoring-batch median imputation with a train-fitted persisted imputer and a per-feature missing-data contract removes holdout leakage and batch dependence WITHOUT making the holdout log loss worse (integrity repair, not a tuning exercise).
baseline: legacy recipe (player_model.model.train recipe=legacy), same data snapshot, same split, same estimators
code_ref: branch r2/props-integrity; exact SHA recorded per run in output/props_r2/props_r2_challengers.json (code_sha)
data: player_history.parquet at the checked-out commit (injury columns point-in-time since 2026-10-26)
training_cutoff: last fit+calibration row of the chronological 80% (split_bounds); recorded per run
blocks: fit 0..68% | calibration 68..80% | untouched holdout 80..100% (chronological, rows sorted by date)
market_metrics: NONE - props are paper permanently; no ROI/EV/staking computed

pass_criteria_frozen.non_inferior: upper 95% week-block bootstrap CI of (repaired - legacy) holdout log loss <= +0.001
pass_criteria_frozen.integrity: tests/test_props_r2_integrity.py passes (batch invariance, fit-block-only statistics, no silent zero)

promotion_criteria: NONE automatic. Passing makes the recipe eligible for SHADOW scoring next to the champion; any serving change requires PG-PROPS + explicit owner approval.
